page.metaDescription: In-depth guide to every feature: dashboard, portfolio, watchlist, alerts, AI analyses, theme baskets, screener, backtest, dividends, data sources, API keys and privacy.
page.title: Help & FAQ
page.intro: An in-depth guide to every feature — from your first login to the AI-powered analyses. Every menu item is described here with its purpose and the result you can expect.
page.indexIntro: Alphabetical list of every term — one click jumps to the matching section.

ersteSchritte.purposeH3: What is AI Stock Analyzer for?
ersteSchritte.purposeP: AI Stock Analyzer is your personal command centre for stocks and ETFs. In a single interface you see your portfolio with live prices and P/L, watch interesting stocks on a watchlist, get notified by alerts when a price breaks a level, and run AI-powered analyses to dig deeper into individual names. On top of that there's dividend planning, a tax overview, screeners for new ideas and market data such as earnings calendar, sentiment and index movers. The site is not investment advice — all content is purely informational and decisions are yours alone.
ersteSchritte.audienceBefore: For retail investors who want to actively track their investments without juggling five different tools. Prior knowledge helps but isn't required: terms like P/E, Sharpe ratio or beta are explained in the
ersteSchritte.audienceAfter: , and help mode (the question mark in the top right) shows explanatory tooltips on every page.

ersteSchritte.needKeyH3: Do I really need an AI key?
ersteSchritte.needKeyP: No. Quotes, watchlist, alerts, dividends, screener, tax reports, performance metrics, the earnings calendar, the market radar (in the data variant) and the live index ticker all work without AI. An AI provider is only needed once you want to deeply analyse individual stocks, run bull/bear comparisons or a DCF, use the chat, weekly briefing, news digest, macro scenarios, theme baskets or the magazine analysis.
ersteSchritte.currencyH3: Display in EUR or original currency?
ersteSchritte.currencyP: Amounts are shown by default in your base currency (typically EUR) so you can compare values across all positions. The original currency is usually shown next to the value or in a tooltip. FX rates are refreshed daily.

dashboard.introAfter: is your home page. It pulls the most important things into one view — at a glance you should immediately see whether anything needs your attention. Tiles refresh automatically every minute during extended trading hours (Mon–Fri 09:00–23:00 CET) as long as the browser tab is in the foreground. A manual reload is usually not needed.
dashboard.listIntro: What you see on the dashboard:
dashboard.item1: Live index ticker at the top of the screen — DAX, Dow Jones, S&P 500, Nikkei, Bitcoin, gold, EUR/USD, Brent. Gives you a feel for the market in two seconds.
dashboard.item2: Portfolio snapshot with total value, today's gain and percentage change. Right below: the biggest daily gainers and losers from your holdings.
dashboard.item3: Watchlist highlights: stocks from your watchlist with notable moves, close to a 52-week high or low.
dashboard.item4: Active alerts and recently triggered: one click takes you to the alert list.
dashboard.item5: Upcoming earnings from your portfolio and watchlist with date and time.
dashboard.item6: Dividend reminders for the coming days and weeks.
dashboard.item7: Sentiment and heatmap widgets (US sectors, commodities, crypto indices), depending on your dashboard settings.
dashboard.footer: Which tiles appear in which order is configurable — open the gear icon on the dashboard to show/hide widgets or to rearrange them by drag-and-drop. The setting is stored per browser.

menu.intro: The top navigation bar shows — depending on screen width — a selection of the most important menu items. The remaining entries live in the More dropdown, grouped into four areas. The chapters of this help describe each menu item in detail; here's a brief overview for orientation:
menu.portfolioAfter: — all your positions with current price, P/L and daily change.
menu.transactionsAfter: — buys and sells as movements; the portfolio is computed from them automatically.
menu.importAfter: — read CSV files from your online banking and create positions.
menu.rebalanceAfter: — define target weights, receive concrete buy/sell suggestions.
menu.riskAfter: — concentration risks, volatility, drawdown risk, worst-case scenarios.
menu.healthAfter: — overall score of your portfolio across diversification, valuation and quality.
menu.metricsAfter: — Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar ratio, max drawdown, monthly returns heatmap.
menu.correlAfter: — correlation matrix of holdings and beta against indices.
menu.reportAfter: — print-ready overview with positions, P/L and diversification.
menu.taxAfter: — realised gains/losses and dividends, exportable as CSV.
menu.alertsAfter: — price and indicator alarms with a history of fired events.
menu.watchlistAfter: — watched stocks with live prices and notes.
menu.communityAfter: — curated lists shared by other users.
menu.dividendsAfter: — received and expected distributions for your portfolio.
menu.divCalAfter: — ex-dates and payment dates as a calendar view.
menu.calAfter: — upcoming quarterly results for your stocks.
menu.marketAfter: — indices worldwide, sector heatmap, top 10 / flop 10 of the major indices.
menu.macroAfter: — rates, inflation, fear & greed, volatility index, commodities.
menu.macroScenarioAfter: — AI-driven what-if analyses for your portfolio under different macro regimes.
menu.insightsAfter: — AI-driven top-down view of your portfolio with concrete recommendations.
menu.chatAfter: — free-form dialogue with the AI about your portfolio and the market.
menu.screenerAfter: — configurable filters (P/E, market cap, sector, country, momentum).
menu.breakoutAfter: — technical screener for stocks close to or just past a 52-week-high breakout.
menu.discoveriesAfter: — AI suggestions for stocks that fit your existing portfolio.
menu.themesAfter: — AI-curated lists around investment themes, sorted by market cap into big, mid and small cap.
menu.digestAfter: — aggregated and summarised news for your stocks.
menu.trackAfter: — evaluation of how previous AI recommendations have actually performed.
menu.magazineAfter: — upload a financial magazine PDF; recommendations are extracted by the AI.
menu.thesenAfter: — write your own thesis per stock and have it reviewed later.
menu.briefingAfter: — weekly summary of the market and your portfolio.
menu.strategiesAfter: — explainers for investment strategies (dividend growth, value, momentum, defensive, etc.).

portfolioSection.overviewAfter: is the table of your holdings: per position you see ticker, name, quantity, average cost, current price, daily change, market value in EUR and absolute / percentage gain or loss. Columns are sortable; clicking the ticker takes you to the stock detail page. Prices auto-refresh every 60 seconds during trading hours.
portfolioSection.manualP: Use the form at the top to enter a new position directly — ticker, quantity, average price, optional notes. The ticker is validated live and the name is auto-completed from the price feed; this guards against typos. The position appears immediately in the table.
portfolioSection.txH3: Working with transactions instead of standing positions
portfolioSection.txBefore: Instead of maintaining a single “I currently hold X shares at avg Y EUR” line, you can record each buy and sell individually in
portfolioSection.txAfter: — with date, quantity, price and fees. The portfolio is then computed automatically using FIFO (first shares bought are sold first), which matters for realistic realised gains and for the tax report. You can freely mix: some positions as standing values, others as transaction series.
portfolioSection.importAfter: to upload a CSV file from your online banking. Trade Republic, comdirect, Consorsbank, ING, DKB, Scalable Capital, finanzen.net Zero and Flatex are among the formats we recognise. Columns are mapped automatically; before saving you see a preview of detected buys, sells and dividends. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
portfolioSection.reportAfter: generates a print-ready overview: every position with current market value, P/L, sector and country breakdown, benchmark comparison (e.g. vs. MSCI World) and your biggest winners and losers over the reporting period. Handy for quarterly documentation or as a printout for tax records.
portfolioSection.taxAfter: lists all realised gains and losses of a calendar year by FIFO plus all received dividends — converted to EUR using the rate of the booking date. You can export the report as CSV and pass it to your tax adviser or tax software. It does not replace tax advice but provides a clean starting point.
portfolioSection.riskAfter: you see where your portfolio is vulnerable: concentration risk (single position too large, sector or country overweight), volatility, historical max drawdown and worst-case scenarios (“what if a 2008-style crash hit today?”). Each finding is flagged with a short reason.
portfolioSection.healthAfter: page condenses risk and quality into one overall score: diversification, valuation (average P/E, forward P/E), quality of the companies (e.g. return on equity, leverage) and a stability indicator (how prone to swings the portfolio is overall). You see at a glance where action is needed.
portfolioSection.metricsAfter: you'll find the standard ratios professionals use to measure portfolios: Sharpe ratio (return per unit of volatility), Sortino ratio (only downside volatility as risk), Calmar ratio (return vs. max drawdown), max drawdown itself, monthly and yearly returns, monthly performance heatmap.
portfolioSection.correlAfter: shows how much your positions move together. A correlation matrix colours pairs green when they tend to move together, red when they move opposite. Highly co-moving positions point to insufficient diversification. Beta against major indices reveals how market-dependent your portfolio is.
portfolioSection.rebAfter: you define target weights for individual positions or entire sectors — for example “US 60%, Europe 30%, emerging markets 10%”. The app compares the actual state with the target and proposes concrete buys and sells to align the portfolio with the target weights, including estimated share counts and EUR amounts.

watchlist.personalAfter: you collect stocks you want to track without owning them. Per entry you see: current price, daily change, distance to the 52-week high and low, sparkline (mini-chart of the last 30 days) and — where available — the conviction score. The conviction score is a 0–100 reading combining analyst recommendations, price targets, valuation and trend strength; higher = more positive. You can add a short note per entry (why is it on the list, what do you expect). Like the portfolio, the watchlist auto-refreshes every minute during trading hours.
watchlist.communityAfter: you can share your own lists with other users or browse theirs — typical themes include “dividend aristocrats”, “AI & semiconductors”, “defensive consumer staples”. One click imports an external list into your own watchlist. Private lists remain visible only to you; whether the sharing feature is enabled at all is controlled centrally by the administrator.

alerts.introAfter: you set alarms that automatically notify you as soon as a defined condition is met. Three alarm types are available:
alerts.up: Price up: “Notify me when AAPL rises above 250 USD.” Useful as a sell trigger.
alerts.down: Price down: “Notify me when SAP falls below 220 EUR.” Useful as a buy trigger or stop-loss.
alerts.indicator: Indicator alerts: technical conditions such as “RSI below 30” (oversold), “RSI above 70” (overbought), “MACD bullish cross”, “SMA golden cross”, “Bollinger band breakout” or “price crosses 200-day line”.
alerts.fireBefore: When an alert fires you receive an email (if email notifications are enabled), an optional browser push notification (can be enabled in settings) and an entry in the
alerts.fireAfter: . The alert is automatically deactivated so it doesn't fire repeatedly; one click rearms it.
alerts.important: Important: Evaluation runs server-side in the background — you don't need to keep the app open. Alerts are also checked overnight and on weekends, as soon as the relevant markets reopen.

detail.intro: Whenever you click a ticker anywhere in the app — in the watchlist, portfolio, a theme basket, the screener — you land on the stock detail page. Here all information about a single stock is bundled. The page is intentionally long and modular: scroll past anything that doesn't interest you, everything is optional. Order of blocks from top to bottom:
detail.headH3: Header with live price and recommendation
detail.headP: Current price in original currency with daily change, market cap, 52-week range and intraday high/low. Next to it a recommendation badge (Buy / Hold / Sell / Reduce / Accumulate) — it summarises aggregated analyst sentiment when data is available. Click the watchlist star to add or remove the stock from your watchlist.
detail.chartP: Interactive price chart with selectable timeframe (1 month, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, 2 years, 5 years). The indicator picker above lets you overlay moving averages (SMA, EMA), RSI, MACD, Bollinger bands and more. An AI-powered reading of the active indicators (“what are they saying right now?”) sits directly below the chart, plus an optional AI image recognition that names the current chart pattern (triangle, cup-and-handle, double bottom, …).
detail.fundamentalsP: Sector, industry, country, business description, P/E, forward P/E, dividend yield, beta, profit margin, analyst consensus and average price target. All values explained in help mode.
detail.sizingP: An AI-assisted helper that suggests how much to invest in the stock given your current portfolio. You pick a risk profile (conservative / moderate / aggressive); the AI returns a concrete EUR amount and share count, target weight percentage, possible alternatives and warnings (e.g. “your sector X is already overweight”).
detail.consensus1: Analyst consensus: number of analysts, average price target with range, distribution of Buy/Hold/Sell recommendations over the past months.
detail.consensus2: Earnings reaction: how has the price reacted on the day of quarterly results over the past 8 quarters? Helps you judge whether the stock tends to rally or sell off into earnings season.
detail.consensus3: Insider activity: SEC filings about purchases and sales by executives and major shareholders. Frequent insider buys at high prices are a bullish signal; broad selling is a warning sign.
detail.proH3: Pro scores, DCF and deep fundamentals
detail.pro1: Pro scores: aggregated point ratings for valuation, growth, profitability, balance sheet and momentum. A quick read on “where does this stock stand?”
detail.pro2: DCF valuation: discounted cash flow model that computes a fair value per share from historical free cash flows. You can adjust growth assumptions and discount rate and immediately see the effect.
detail.pro3: Deep fundamentals: extended balance-sheet and P&L metrics (return on equity, free cash flow, debt/EBITDA, payout ratio, …) with multi-year trends.
detail.thesis1: Bull/bear: the AI argues in two columns why you would buy and why you would stay away. Helps you stress-test your own thesis for consistency.
detail.thesis2: Investment thesis: you can articulate your own core thesis for the stock (“I expect X by Q3”). The entry price is captured; later the AI can review the thesis against actual price action.
detail.thesis3: Notes: personal notes visible only to you — see the next chapter.
detail.relationsP: The relationship map shows the company's business graph: key customers, suppliers, partners, competitors, subsidiaries and investees. This surfaces second-order effects: who else profits or suffers when this stock moves.
detail.att1: Wikipedia: daily page views of the company's English Wikipedia page as an indicator of public interest. Spikes often precede news.
detail.att2: Google Trends: worldwide search queries for the company or ticker name.
detail.att3: Reddit buzz: recent Reddit threads from investing subreddits mentioning the ticker — with sentiment tendency and link to the discussion.
detail.newsP: The ten most recent relevant news items about the company, sorted chronologically. One click opens the source.

notes.intro: Every stock detail page contains a notes block. Use it to capture thoughts, observations and expectations on the stock — visible only to you. Typical content:
notes.i1: Earnings expectation: “I don't expect growth in Q1 because they cut the marketing budget in early 2025.”
notes.i2: Exit condition: “Sell at 250 EUR or if gross margin drops below 40%.”
notes.i3: Observation: “CEO change announced for mid-2026 — review impact.”
notes.footer: Notes are free text (up to 5,000 characters) and timestamped. You can pin important notes so they always appear on top. The modification date is shown when you edit; deletion only happens after confirmation. You can also attach notes to stocks that aren't in your portfolio or watchlist — for example to document why you decided not to invest.

market.radarAfter: is the bird's-eye view of the current market action. It shows:
market.r1: The most important indices worldwide (DAX, MDAX, SDAX, TecDAX, Xetra, Dow Jones, S&P 500, Nasdaq 100, Nikkei) with daily, weekly and monthly changes.
market.r2: Top 10 / Flop 10: the biggest daily gainers and losers per index — a fast way to spot action. A server-side refresh on an adjustable interval keeps the lists current for every user.
market.r3: A colour-coded sector heatmap at the US-sector level so you can see at a glance where money is flowing today.
market.r4: Optional AI commentary: two or three sentences on which themes are driving the market today.
market.macroAfter: we bundle the economic and sentiment indicators almost every market observer keeps an eye on:
market.m1: Rates & yield curve: 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year US Treasury yields and the spread (10y–2y). An inverted curve has historically been a recession leading indicator.
market.m2: Inflation: current CPI and core CPI with year-over-year comparison.
market.m5: Sentiment: Fear & Greed index, AAII investor sentiment.
market.m6: Commodities & crypto: gold, silver, Brent, WTI, Bitcoin, Ether.
market.scenarioAfter: you play what-if questions through for your portfolio. The AI describes three or four alternative regimes (e.g. “soft landing”, “stagflation”, “recession”, “expansion”) and estimates which positions win or lose in each — including concrete suggestions such as reweighting or hedges.
market.earningsAfter: shows all upcoming quarterly results for your positions and watchlist. Per entry: date, time (before/after the close), expected EPS/revenue and the prior-quarter value. You can pull important dates into your phone's calendar via an alert.

dividends.personalAfter: you see per position: dividends actually received so far, the expected next payment with date, yield on cost (the dividend yield on your entry price) and the expected gross dividends for the next 12 months. Amounts are converted to EUR with the original currency shown next to them.
dividends.calendarAfter: lays out ex-dates and pay dates for the coming weeks chronologically. So you know when each stock pays and when the cash hits the account.
dividends.topAfter: is a curated screener for stocks with high and/or growing distribution yields. You can filter by sector, region and minimum yield. The underlying data is shared — once one user scans, the rest benefit until the next scan.

find.screenerAfter: is the standard tool for the idea “which stocks currently match the following criteria?”. You can combine freely:
find.s1: Valuation: P/E range, forward P/E, price-to-book, dividend yield.
find.s3: Region & sector: USA / Europe / Asia; sector and industry selection.
find.s5: Quality: return on equity, gross margin, leverage.
find.screenerFooter: You can save commonly used filter combinations as a set and rerun them with one click.
find.breakoutAfter: finds stocks on the brink of a technical breakout or just past one: near their 52-week high, with a volume spike and solid trend quality. Optionally you can layer in fundamental and alternative data sources (insider buying, attention signals) so the picture isn't purely technical.
find.peerAfter: you line up to eight stocks side by side. Columns show fundamental metrics (P/E, dividend yield, margins, leverage) and technical metrics (1/3/12-month performance, distance to highs and lows) simultaneously — ideal for choosing between several candidates in the same sector.
find.discAfter: the AI proposes stocks that fit your existing portfolio or would fill a gap — for example because you currently lack semiconductors, healthcare or European value stocks. Suggestions come with a short rationale; interesting names can be added directly to your watchlist or analysed deeper.

themes.introAfter: are curated stock lists around an investment theme. You briefly describe what interests you — e.g. “AI semiconductors”, “European defence”, “water utilities”, “demographics & care” — and the AI suggests around 30 fitting stocks. The suggestions are then validated against the price data (stocks that don't exist or lack a market cap are filtered out automatically) and sorted into three columns:
themes.big: Big cap — heavyweights with a market value of more than USD 50 bn. Stable, widely traded, often part of an index.
themes.mid: Mid cap — established companies with USD 5–50 bn market value. Often the sweet spot between growth and stability.
themes.small: Small / mini cap — smaller companies below USD 5 bn market value. Riskier but with greater growth potential.
themes.buckets: Per bucket you get up to 10 stocks with name, USD market cap and a one-sentence rationale for why the AI placed them in the theme. Clicking the ticker takes you to the stock detail page.
themes.regenerate: You can always regenerate a theme via “Regenerate” — useful when the list is older and the market landscape has shifted. Personal themes are visible only to you; the administrator can additionally provide default baskets visible to everyone. Because every run consumes AI tokens, a refresh usually only pays off every few weeks.

ai.providerP: AI Stock Analyzer supports multiple providers and all deliver usable results. Our experience in a nutshell:
ai.p1: Claude (Anthropic): very careful, structured analysis — particularly strong at long contexts and multi-step reasoning. A good default.
ai.p2: Gemini (Google): cheap or free at entry tier, strong at quantitative reasoning.
ai.p3: Groq: extremely fast responses thanks to specialised hardware, great for many small iterations. Limited at very long contexts.
ai.p4: OpenAI: solid all-rounder with a good model lineup.
ai.providerFooterAfter: . If the administrator has shared a common key, you can also use AI features without your own key, within a daily/monthly limit.
ai.insightsH3: Insights — AI view of the whole portfolio
ai.insightsAfter: the AI analyses your entire portfolio in one pass: concentration risks, diversification gaps, notable valuations, potential add-ons and sell candidates. Unlike single-stock analysis, Insights provides a top-down perspective — what should I tackle in the portfolio today, what already fits?
ai.chatH3: Chat — talk freely with your portfolio
ai.chatAfter: you can converse freely with the AI about your portfolio. The AI has the context of your positions, watchlist, the current market and your settings — so you can ask things like “what's my US weight?”, “which of my stocks are most oversold right now?”, “should I add SAP or rather BASF?”. You can refresh the context at any time with one click if you just changed positions.
ai.digestAfter: reads news for every stock in your portfolio and (optionally) your watchlist over a configurable window, summarises them and groups them by relevance and sentiment. You can have the digest emailed to you on a schedule, daily or weekly.
ai.briefingAfter: is a short document generated weekly that summarises the most important market themes, moves in your portfolio, upcoming earnings and macro events of the next week — like a newsletter, but tailored to your portfolio.
ai.trackBefore: How good have the AI recommendations been in hindsight? On
ai.trackAfter: you see the performance of past recommendations: at what price was it issued, what is the price today, how would Buy / Hold / Sell have played out. The track record helps you assess the AI realistically — it isn't infallible, but its hit rate becomes transparent.
ai.backtestAfter: you simulate strategies historically. Examples: “Savings plan: EUR 200 / month into MSCI World since 2010”, “Quarterly rebalance to 60/40”, “Buy on RSI < 30, sell on RSI > 70”. You get end value, annualised return, max drawdown and an equity curve next to the buy-and-hold variant of the same investment.
ai.magazineAfter: you upload the PDF of a financial magazine (Der Aktionär, Börse Online, Focus Money, Effecten-Spiegel, etc.). The AI extracts all recommendations, groups them into Buy / Hold / Sell / Accumulate / Reduce and checks which of the recommended stocks are already in your portfolio. You get a tidy table instead of 80 pages of reading. If the administrator enabled sharing, you can publish analyses for other users as well.
ai.thesenAfter: you get an overview of all the theses you've articulated on the stock detail pages. A thesis has an expectation anchor (e.g. “30% higher by mid-2026 if margins hold”) and an entry price. The AI later helps you check the thesis against actual price action — either “keep holding”, “thesis missed, time to exit” or “thesis achieved, refine the plan”.

content.stratAfter: you'll find explainers on classic investment styles — dividend growth, value investing, momentum, defensive, ETF savings plan, quality. Per strategy: core principle, typical metrics, example stocks and potential pitfalls. Useful for sharpening your own investment philosophy before filtering in the screener.
content.glossAfter: is an encyclopaedia of every financial term that appears in the app — from P/E to Sortino ratio, from yield on cost to Kelly criterion. Alphabetically sorted, each with a short definition, example and (where appropriate) the formula.
content.modeP: When you toggle the question-mark icon in the top right of the navigation bar, every page shows small explanatory tooltips on cards and controls. That way you get help right where you are — without having to search this FAQ. Click again to switch the mode off.

apiKeys.intro: You need an API key as soon as you want to use AI features with your own account at the AI provider — either because the administrator has not shared a common key or because you've hit your assigned limit. You can store multiple keys side by side and switch providers in settings at any time. All keys are stored encrypted and are not cached in the browser.
apiKeys.billingNotice: Billing note: AI request costs are billed directly by the provider (Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, Groq, …) — not through AI Stock Analyzer. Be sure to set a spend limit or budget at the provider so you don't accidentally spend more than planned. The app shows your usage and estimated costs in parallel.
apiKeys.claude1After: and create an account. First sign-up requires an email address and a mobile phone number.
apiKeys.claude2: Top up a credit under Settings → Billing — in our experience five dollars are enough for many hundred single analyses. Set a spend limit right below so there are no nasty surprises.
apiKeys.claude3: Create a new key under Settings → API Keys → Create Key. It starts with “sk-ant-” and is visible only once — copy it immediately.
apiKeys.claude4After: , choose provider Claude and paste the key. Recommended models: claude-sonnet-4-6 for most uses or claude-opus-4-7 for the deepest analyses (significantly more expensive).
apiKeys.gemini1After: and sign in with a Google account.
apiKeys.gemini2: Click Create API key. Optionally you can bind the key to an existing Google Cloud project — for private use the default is fine.
apiKeys.gemini3Before: Copy the key (typically starts with “AIza”) and paste it in
apiKeys.gemini3After: under provider Gemini. Recommended models: gemini-2.5-pro for detailed analyses, gemini-2.5-flash for faster responses.
apiKeys.geminiFooter: Gemini offers a generous free tier that is usually enough for occasional use.
apiKeys.groq1After: . Sign-in with Google or GitHub is possible.
apiKeys.groq2: Create a key under API Keys → Create API Key (starts with “gsk_”).
apiKeys.groq3After: choose the provider OpenAI-compatible, enter https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 as base URL, paste the key and configure a model such as llama-3.3-70b-versatile.
apiKeys.groqFooter: Groq is free at entry tier (with rate limits) and responds very quickly. Less suitable for very long contexts like the magazine analysis — use Claude or Gemini there.
apiKeys.openai1After: and sign in. New accounts must top up a credit first.
apiKeys.openai2: Set a hard limit under Billing → Usage Limits (e.g. USD 10 per month) — this prevents surprises.
apiKeys.openai3: Use Create new secret key to generate a key (starts with “sk-”). Visible only once — copy immediately.
apiKeys.openai4After: choose provider OpenAI, paste the key and configure a model such as gpt-4o-mini (cheap) or gpt-4.1.
apiKeys.warning: Important: Never share your API keys with others. If a key falls into the wrong hands, delete it immediately at the provider and create a new one.

data.freshnessP: Price data comes from public market feeds and is typically delayed 15 to 20 minutes. During extended trading hours (Mon–Fri 09:00–23:00 CET) server-side caches are refreshed in the background — you don't need to keep the page open. On portfolio, watchlist and dashboard the display additionally refreshes every minute while the tab is in the foreground; when you come back to the tab after a longer break, a fresh load is triggered immediately. Outside trading hours there's no refresh — prices aren't moving anyway.
data.s1: Quotes, fundamentals, charts, news: primarily from Yahoo Finance, with alternative sources as fallback. If one source fails, another is tried automatically.
data.s2: FX conversion: daily rates from a public FX provider, kept in the server cache.
data.s3: Dividends: from each stock's dividend history. The top list is held in common for every user.
data.s4: Insider activity: SEC mandatory filings (Form 4) — i.e. purchases and sales by executives and major shareholders of US-listed companies.
data.s5: Macro data: rates, inflation, labour market from the FRED database of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.
data.s6: Attention signals: Wikipedia page views, Google Trends search index, Reddit posts from investing subreddits. These signals are not investment advice but a useful leading indicator for media attention.
data.s7: Live index ticker (DAX, Dow, S&P 500, Nikkei, Bitcoin, gold, EUR/USD, Brent): from the regular market feed, refreshed more often than the standard quotes.
data.fallbackH3: What happens when a data source fails?
data.fallbackP: If a source fails or is too slow, the app automatically tries an alternative — at worst you see a subtle notice that a certain piece of information is currently not up to date. The rest of the page continues to work normally.

account.exportAfter: under “Your data” you'll find a button “Request data export”. You receive a JSON file with all records stored for your account — positions, transactions, watchlist, notes, alerts, investment theses, backtests, notes, magazine analyses and so on. For security reasons your password hash and the encrypted API keys are not part of the export.
account.deleteP: Also in settings you'll find the option “Delete account”. For security your password is asked for once more. Deletion is immediate and irreversible — all your positions, transactions, watchlists, alerts, investment theses, notes, magazine analyses, backtests, theme baskets and AI histories are removed. If you are the sole administrator of the system, deletion is blocked — please add another administrator first.
account.cookiesP: The site sets only one strictly-necessary session cookie to keep you logged in. There is no tracking, no third-party cookies, no advertising pixels. The cookie banner is purely informational.

security.twofaAfter: under “Security” you can enable two-factor authentication via an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password, Bitwarden, Microsoft Authenticator, …). When you activate it you receive a QR code to scan and afterwards recovery codes — keep the recovery codes somewhere safe, they let you regain access even if you lose your phone. Without a 2FA code and without a recovery code, login is no longer possible.
security.resetP: The login page has a “Forgot password” link. Enter your email address; you'll receive an email with a reset link at the address on file. The link is time-limited.
security.keysP: Your own AI API keys are stored encrypted and are never sent back to the browser. They are used only to send your AI requests to the configured provider — never for display, never for comparison, never for sharing.
